newsitem.title: UK: LME copper gains foothold over $2,400, spreads fir.
newsitem.headline: LME copper gains foothold over $2,400, spreads fir.

text.p: LME copper hurdled the $2,400 barrier on speculative buying in early business on Monday morning, and later ring activity is expected to be heated as tight dates come to the fore, traders said.
"We saw decent tonnage moving this morning as the specs pushed it over $2,400 and tried for upside stops," one said.
Three months skated to $2,405, up $22 from the Friday afternoon kerb close, but ran into steady profit-taking and forward selling, traders said.
"Now it's struggling to maintain $2,400," a trader said.
Supporting the move was a stocks fall of 3,400 tonnes.

Only 600 tonnes moved into LME warehouses, while 4,000 tonnes exited, confounding expectations that players would be keen to put tonnage under LME warrant to take advantage of the flaring backwardation.
Some traders had suggested that it would be easy to move Comex metal into the LME's Long Beach warehouse, but the latter showed a net decline on Monday of 200 tonnes.
The bulk of the withdrawal came from the LME Singapore warehouse, at a net draw of 2,750 tonnes. Last week, stocks declined there by a net 4,425 tonnes.
"Reports from China do suggest a tightening of the domestic market since the first quarter, when an inventory overhang from last year weighed on the market," Macquarie Equities said in a commentary.
The cash/threes backwardation was standing at $210/$215 in early activity, a touch wider from $200/$210 on Friday.
The tight April 30 date will be traded as cash in ring
trading and the cash/next day spread is expected to move towards the LME-imposed limit.
The limit, at a $26 backwardation on Monday, is one percent of the previous day's cash settlement.
"I can see it trying $20. People who are long will be likely to lend it above $20," a trader said.
Aluminium also surged after a strong close on Friday, knocking down resistance at $1,625 and probing the next barrier at $1,642.
The market settled at $1,641, up $28, after stocks fell by 2,650 tonnes.
More borrowing was seen on Monday morning and the cash/threes spread was slightly narrower at a $25/$22 contango compared to $27/$26 on Friday evening and around $32 the previous day.
The other metals followed copper and aluminium higher.
Nickel broke through $7,500, settling $50 higher at $7,530.
Resistance was seen at the 30-day moving average around $7,600.
Zinc added $5 to $1,280, with resistance seen at last week's highs of $1,285/88.
Lead gained $9 to $640, but a solid wall of resistance was expected at $644/5.
Tin was only $10 firmer at $5,750 and had a long way to go before challenging last week's peak of $5,840.
Alloy was stronger at $1,515 after $1,490/95 on Friday.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
